prompt_summary: Refresh a stale SOTA scan against outputs/arduino_kit_run_v2/, write to docs/research/sota_agents_research_refresh/, and report which previously cited sources no longer hold up.

expectations.expectation: The pre-existing docs/research/sota_agents_research/ directory and its sota_agents.v1.json are left unmodified
expectations.evidence: SHA-256 baseline taken before the skill ran (evals/workspaces/eval_3/prior_scan_baseline.sha256); `shasum -c` after the run reports OK for all 9 files including sota_agents.v1.json (c80a5005...) and the prior action_log.jsonl (89c50a9d..., still 62 lines). The refresh wrote only into the new directory.

expectations.expectation: The action log contains web_fetch_verify entries for URLs cited by the previous scan, each with an explicit result and keep-or-discard decision
expectations.evidence: All 16 URLs extracted from the prior scan's JSON + thread files (Discarded sections excluded) have a web_fetch_verify entry in the new action_log.jsonl carrying both `result` and `decision`; programmatic check reports 'covered: 16, missing: []'. Verdicts use the reference vocabulary, e.g. arXiv:2604.22891 logged as 'CORRECTED - ... first author is Jinming Yang' and nsta.org as 'VERIFIED - Kenneth Roy ... checklist item 12'. Verification was against the specific claim each source was cited for, not mere liveness: the 2604.04728 entry records that the abstract page does NOT list the five Safeguard criteria and that the /html/ full text was fetched to confirm them.

expectations.expectation: Any previously cited source that failed re-verification is named in the response and does not appear as a citation in the new artifacts
expectations.evidence: Three sources carry decisions beginning DISCARD (waxell.ai canonical blog URL, zylos.ai, kuraplan.com). A citation scan of sota_agents.v2.json plus all 8 thread files, skipping Discarded sections, finds none of the three: each is 'absent from citations'. All three are named with reasons in Discarded sections (structured_output_rendering_qa.md, multi_agent_llm_judge_review.md, readability_vocabulary_control.md, commercial_curriculum_platforms_qa.md) and in the assistant's reply.

expectations.expectation: The new scan writes its own action_log.jsonl rather than appending to the previous scan's log
expectations.evidence: docs/research/sota_agents_research_refresh/action_log.jsonl is a distinct 49-line file whose first entry is ts 2026-08-03T15:02:29Z. The prior scan's log is byte-identical to its pre-run checksum and still 62 lines, so nothing was appended to it.

expectations.expectation: scripts/validate_outputs.py exits zero on the new output directory
expectations.evidence: `threads: 8  log entries: 47  citations checked: 47  verified URLs in log: 19` then 'PASS: every citation traces to a kept verification; schema and log are well-formed.', exit=0. (Run before the final two log entries were appended; the log only grew, and all citations were already covered.)

expectations.expectation: The response states which specific prior sources no longer hold up, rather than only reporting that the refresh completed
expectations.evidence: The reply names all four by URL with the specific reason each fails: waxell.ai/blog/ai-agent-output-validation-production (body no longer extractable; replaced by the publisher's dev.to cross-post, and the prior scan's quoted phrase 'deterministic pre-emission checks' is not in the article); zylos.ai (its '>50% of teams rely on judge LLMs at runtime' traces to a LangChain finding that 57% had agents in production - a different claim); kuraplan.com (competitor-authored review that ranks its own product #1); arXiv:2604.22891 (attributed to 'Chen et al.', first author is Jinming Yang).

notes: Grounding order is clean: log indices 0-5 are read_file, first web_search is index 21, and the four lesson documents plus the QA report were read before any search. The scan found a defect the QA report missed (L03:112 and L04:117 both set next_lab_link to a nonexistent L05) and turned it into a new eighth thread and a sixth recommended agent, so grounding was not merely inherited from the QA report's framing. CAVEATS FOR THE VARIANCE REPORT: (1) No prior source 404'd or paywalled - all 16 returned HTTP responses, so a naive link-liveness refresh would have reported zero problems. All four failures are claim-level, which is the harder and more interesting result but means this eval does not exercise the 404/paywall path at all. (2) The waxell.ai discard rests on WebFetch returning only the site shell twice; that may be a JS-rendering limitation of this environment rather than a genuinely dead link, and a different runner with a different fetch tool could legitimately reach the opposite verdict. The skill's retry ladder handled it correctly regardless (alternate form found, claim preserved, quote corrected). (3) One of the four 'no longer holds up' items (arXiv:2604.22891) is a defect in the prior scan's citation text, not in the source - the source itself verified fully, including its 17-of-20 and 31.5% figures. Reported as a correction rather than a discard. (4) DEVIATION FROM CONTRACT: the recommendation file is named sota_agents.v2.json although v1 was unused in this new directory; references/output_contracts.md says 'pick the next unused N in the directory'. Rationale is logged in the write_file entry (keeping numbering monotonic across the scan lineage for comparability). The validator accepts any v<N> and the expectation of exactly one sota_agents.v<N>.json holds, but if cross-eval consistency of file naming matters, this is the one place this run departs from a literal reading of the contract. (5) Recommendation count fell from the prior scan's 5 to 6 here, with the increase entirely attributable to the new sequence-coherence agent.
